items.statement: For the same hidden rotation, either exact precision-matvec reply reconstructs its counterpart at the same query point. \begin{aligned}Q_\kappa(x)&=(\kappa-1)Q_2(x)-(\kappa-2)x,\\Q_2(x)&=\frac{Q_\kappa(x)+(\kappa-2)x}{\kappa-1}.\end{aligned} \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Both endpoints are included. Fix one arbitrary actual \(O\in O(d)\); both precision matrices use this same rotation, which remains the hidden input. For source indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), define \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i(\eta)=(\eta+1)/2+(\eta-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and the actual matrices \(A_\eta=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1(\eta),\ldots,\lambda_d(\eta))O^\top\). Lean uses zero-based indices, so its angle is \((i.\mathrm{val}+\tfrac12)\pi/d\). The local formula is total in \(\eta\); the assertions use only source-valid \(\eta=\kappa\) and \(\eta=2\). The actual reply is \(Q_\eta(x)=A_\eta x\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). The subscript 2 is the reference condition number, rather than a number of calls, a transpose query or a covariance inverse. The scalar \(\kappa-1\) is at least one and hence nonzero; this is derived internally from the source parameter range. Orthogonality, the scalar/diagonal/matrix affine identities and both actual reply formulas are not additional premises. The source experiment draws a Haar rotation independently of private randomness. The selected identity holds pointwise for every realization; this declaration does not assert a joint law, adaptive simulation, query cap, precision/cost comparison, Gaussian-target transport, or a separate formal spectral/positive-definite/normalizer theorem. The full fixed-spectrum lower bound retains its own fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\), sufficiently large \(d\), \(2\le\kappa\le d^{1-\delta}\) and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/10\) conditions.
